web_blocks.text: What Adobe Does & Why This Monograph Exists Today
web_blocks.title: What Adobe Does & Why This Monograph Exists Today

web_blocks.html: Adobe Inc. (NASDAQ: ADBE) is the global standard for creative tools, digital documents, and enterprise marketing workflows. Over forty-four years, it built a 97%-recurring subscription engine spanning Creative Cloud, Acrobat, Firefly AI, GenStudio, and Adobe Experience Platform. In 2026, Adobe added Semrush ($1.9B, April 2026) and Topaz Labs (September 2026) to widen that footprint [16, 18]. FY2025 revenue reached $23,769M, and LTM revenue hit $25,970M (+12.03% YoY) through Q3 FY2026 [1, 4]. Gross margins stand at 89.3%, FY2025 GAAP operating margins at 36.6%, LTM GAAP free cash flow at $10,592M, LTM FCF ex-SBC at $8,521M, and ROIC at 43.25% [1, 4, 25]. Yet ADBE shares have dropped 64.94% over five years to $232.08 as of November 24, 2026 ($91.43B market cap). At 8.50x forward P/E and 10.7x LTM FCF ex-SBC, the market prices in a -1.61% annual owner-earnings shrink for ten straight years.

web_blocks.text: The Core Debate & Our Independent Dual Verdict
web_blocks.title: The Core Debate & Our Independent Dual Verdict

web_blocks.html: Our price-blind audit (Chapters 1–6) awards Adobe COMPOUNDER_PASS quality, but sets KPI health to PASS_WITH_WATCH. Five concrete risks explain the valuation discount. First, Q3 FY2026 brought Adobe's first sequential RPO dip in eight years (-$110M to $22.16B, +8.4% YoY) plus a -$46M deferred-revenue drag [4, 22]. Second, Adobe pivoted to freemium user acquisition and deferred Creative Cloud price hikes in June 2026 while Canva made Affinity free forever. Third, AI inference pushed Q3 Subscription COGS up +24.1% YoY, trimming GAAP and Non-GAAP operating margins by 150–230 bps [4, 6]. Fourth, CEO Shantanu Narayen hands over to Anil Chakravarthy on December 1, 2026, while Steve Day serves as interim CFO ahead of December 9 earnings [23]. Fifth, Adobe paid $150M in March 2026 to settle the DOJ/FTC subscription lawsuit [14].

Our 10%-WACC owner-earnings DCF sets Base fair value at $317.11 (+36.6%) (or $270.81 normalized to $7,284M GAAP Net Income). Bear fair value is $174.15 (-25.0%), Bull is $484.30 (+108.7%), and probability-weighted expected value is $314.81 (+35.6%). Even so, ADBE sits in confirmed Weinstein Stage 4 (CAP_REJECTED) below its 50-day ($242.39), 30-week ($242.92), and 200-day ($245.97) averages inside a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend. Our Dual Verdict is clear. For New Capital, we assign WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT and add ADBE to the active US Shortlist (TIER_3 / CORE_ALPHA). The watch shelf is $216.95–$227.45 with a $204.68 stop (3.94:1 shelf-retest R:R; 1.72:1 on a Stage 2 breakout >$246.00 vs. $204.68). For Current Equity, the action is NOT_HELD (0 shares in Schwab and Robinhood). For Open Options, we flag 2 breached Robinhood $350 Jun-2027 LEAPS calls (ADBE270617C00350000) as CLOSE. Finally, we keep 100% of marginal cash in USD (0% XLV, 0% ADSK) until market breadth improves.

web_blocks.takeaway: Adobe offers rare 43%-ROIC value at 8.5x forward earnings, earning an active Shortlist slot—but Stage 4 tape, a US Downtrend, and December's CEO handover + earnings print demand patience over heroics.

book_paragraphs: Every few years, the public equity market hands patient investors a fascinating puzzle: a household-name software franchise with nearly 90% gross margins, over 43% return on invested capital, and more than $10.5 billion in annual free cash flow suddenly gets priced like a dying legacy utility. As of the verified November 24, 2026 market close, Adobe Inc. trades at $232.08 per share—down 65% over five years, at 8.50x forward earnings and 10.7x true SBC-adjusted owner earnings ($8,521 million LTM). Our Reverse DCF shows that $232.08 literally prices Adobe's owner earnings to shrink at -1.61% per year for the next decade, even though Adobe just grew Q3 FY2026 revenue 12.9% and Total ARR 11.2% to $27.50 billion.

You and I are going to resist both knee-jerk reactions that trap retail investors: we will neither blindly cheerlead 'cheap 8.5x P/E' into a falling knife, nor lazily dismiss Adobe as 'dead to AI.' Instead, this ten-chapter monograph separates business reality from market pricing. Chapters 1 through 6 were written strictly price-blind—evaluating Adobe's forty-four-year history, its real-world customer workflows across Creative, Document, and Experience Cloud, its $100 revenue-to-free-cash-flow waterfall, its fierce battle against Canva's free Affinity suite, Figma, and generative AI video/image upstarts, and its ten-year financial forensics. That blind audit awarded Adobe COMPOUNDER_PASS quality, but flagged five urgent watch items (PASS_WITH_WATCH): the first sequential RPO dip in eight years (-$110 million in Q3 FY2026), AI GPU inference pushing Subscription COGS up 24%, a June 2026 freemium pivot that deferred price hikes, a $150 million DOJ/FTC settlement, and a simultaneous CEO handover (Anil Chakravarthy succeeding Shantanu Narayen on December 1, 2026) alongside an interim CFO.

Only after locking that business verdict did we open valuation (Chapter 7), the Stage 4 weekly chart (Chapter 8), and our two-sided decision framework (Chapter 9). Our conservative 10%-WACC Base Case values Adobe at $317.11 (+36.6%), with Bear at $174.15 (-25.0%), Bull at $484.30 (+108.7%), and probability-weighted expected value at $314.81 (+35.6%). Yet the tape is unforgiving: Adobe sits in Weinstein Stage 4 beneath its 50-day ($242.39), 30-week ($242.92), and 200-day ($245.97) moving averages inside a 10-distribution-day S&P 500 Downtrend. Our verdict is therefore crystal clear: add Adobe to your active US Shortlist at WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (TIER_3, CORE_ALPHA), hold 100% of marginal cash in USD until December 9 Q4 FY2026 earnings and the $246 Stage 2 reclaim line prove institutions are back, note that you hold 0 equity shares (NOT_HELD), and close the 2 breached Robinhood June 2027 $350 Call LEAPS contracts to salvage remaining time value. Let us begin in Chapter 1.

book_callouts.text: Read Chapters 1 through 6 as if Adobe were a private business with no ticker symbol. Then read Chapters 7 through 9 to see how Wall Street's fear around AI seat compression and leadership turnover created an 8.5x forward-P/E dislocation—and why Stage 2 technical discipline keeps us safely in cash until the chart confirms our fundamental thesis.
